solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supports small section of orchestra

blocks.note: bras are garments that support
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A minor part of an orchestra props up the rest of the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' looks like a verb with 'small section' as its object, but it is a plural noun for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass are the trumpets, horns and trombones, one of the instrument families seated together in an orchestra.

clue.text: Jerk over time promises to be overbearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing over another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: a bump is a sudden jolt
T is the usual abbreviation for time
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps making promises over time comes across as pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumptious describes someone self-assertive and conceited in an irritating, overbearing way; the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Wade quietly lost in daze

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so the letter for the quiet word drops out

blocks.note: to paddle is to wade in shallow water
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone wades through water quietly, lost in a dreamy daze.
explanation.walkthrough: PADDLE without its P leaves ADDLE; 'daze' is read as a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle someone is to muddle or confuse their mind, the same as dazing or befuddling them.

clue.text: Upcoming quarrels about the French leading commodities

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom towards the top
about means going around, so the quarrels surround the French article

blocks.note: spats are petty quarrels
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Coming disputes over French goods that dominate the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Staples are the main or most important goods produced or traded, so they are the principal items of commerce.

clue.text: Prevent Nottingham team getting everything

blocks.note: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, usually just called Forest
all means everything

explanation.surface: A football side stops its rivals from winning every trophy going.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is a football club from the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall something is to act in advance so that it cannot happen, which is to stop or preclude it.

clue.text: Insubstantial zip holding this person’s stomach at first

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so the zip wraps around the other pieces
at first points to only the opening letter of the word stomach being used

blocks.note: a fly is the zip or buttoned opening on trousers
this person is the setter, so this person's is read as I am, shortened
the opening letter of stomach

explanation.surface: A flimsy trouser zip barely holds in the wearer's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's here stands for is, not possession: I'M (I am) plus S go inside FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy means weak and lacking solidity, as does insubstantial; both describe something easily broken or torn.

clue.text: Famous name possessed by engineers

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
N is a standard abbreviation for name
owned means possessed

explanation.surface: A well-known name has been bought up by a firm of engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Engineers is a corps of the British Army; 'by' here means beside, so the engineers simply stand at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means widely known and celebrated, a direct synonym of famous.

clue.text: Calms boyfriend wearing specs occasionally

indicators.note: someone wearing a garment is inside it, so the boyfriend goes within the other letters
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of specs is used

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of specs
a date is the person you are going out with

explanation.surface: A boyfriend who only sometimes wears his glasses has a soothing effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedates means gives a drug or treatment to make someone tranquil, which calms them.

clue.text: Exactly an hour after noon people start to try for redemption

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of the word try

blocks.note: one o'clock exactly is one hour after midday, so the phrase is at one
men are people
the opening letter of try

explanation.surface: At precisely one o'clock, people begin trying to save their souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for wrongdoing, through which a sinner is redeemed, so it is a close synonym of redemption.

clue.text: Catalogues inclines

blocks.note: first meaning: itemises, writes down one after another
second meaning: leans over to one side, as a ship does

explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are verbs here, though 'Catalogues' also suggests a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to record items in order and, of a ship, to heel over or tilt sideways.

clue.text: Peacemaking process I dominate corruptly

indicators.note: corruptly means in a debased way, so the letters are spoiled from their proper arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dishonest negotiator boasts of controlling the peace talks unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is intervention by a neutral party to settle a dispute, the process of making peace between sides.

clue.text: Tears heads of dainty rare orchids planted somewhere

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only those are taken from the following words

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A gardener weeps over delicate, uncommon orchids set in some spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' looks like a verb about ripping, but it is the noun for what falls from the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears are small liquid drops falling from the eyes, so the plural noun for droplets matches.

clue.text: Tell sir about framework

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or scattered, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to tell a gentleman about a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of crossed wooden or metal strips supporting climbing plants, a light open frame.

clue.text: See comedian by headland

blocks.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness place names

explanation.surface: Go and watch a stand-up comic performing on a clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a verb here, not a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness an event is to observe it happen in person, which is to see it.

clue.text: Resist work model

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a numbered musical work
to pose is to model for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A fashion model refuses to take on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to fight against it or stand firm against it, so a synonym of resisting.

clue.text: Chippy Roman I annoyed conceals fiery passion

indicators.note: to conceal something is to keep it inside, out of sight, so the answer lies within the preceding words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Chippy, all of Roman and I, and the start of annoyed

explanation.surface: An irritable, touchy Roman hides a burning obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: Chippy is British slang for touchy or resentful, and also a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is an obsessive compulsion to start fires, literally an urge for burning, so a fire-related obsession.

clue.text: Eels lash around hermit crab’s shelter

indicators.note: around suggests letters thrown about here and there, into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Eels thrash about near a hermit crab's home on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermit crabs have soft bodies and live inside the empty shells of sea snails, using them as protective homes.

clue.text: Obtains cloak showing rural picture

blocks.note: to land something is to secure or win it
a cape is a sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a cloak featuring a pastoral scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting depicting countryside scenery, so it is a picture of the rural outdoors.

clue.text: Show about core of overseas U-turn

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for show goes around the middle letters
the core of a word is its centre, so only the central letters of overseas are used

blocks.note: to reveal is to show
the two central letters of overseas

explanation.surface: A show about the heart of foreign affairs announces a policy change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a theatre noun but works as the verb reveal.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a complete change of direction or policy, which is a reversal of course.

clue.text: Showed indifference as second husband gets rough

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies
rugged means rough, as of terrain

explanation.surface: A woman is unbothered when her second husband turns coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders and letting them drop is a gesture meaning you don't care, so it displays indifference.

clue.text: Criminal rogue taking in constant and ardent fan

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order
taking in means absorbing something within, so the constant goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
pi is the mathematical constant for a circle's ratio

explanation.surface: A crooked rascal steadily woos someone devoted to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A groupie is a devoted follower of a band or celebrity, typically one who trails them on tour.

clue.text: Garment made of tin covering behind

indicators.note: something covering another goes over and around it, so the tin encloses the other piece

blocks.note: a tin is a can
aft means at the back, on a ship

explanation.surface: An item of clothing fashioned from metal covers someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made of tin' tempts a solver to build the answer from TIN; tin is the word for a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A caftan is a long loose tunic of Middle Eastern origin, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Job in beer for crusader

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the job sits within the beer

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A job working in a pub suits someone on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' might suggest the biblical figure, but here it is ordinary employment.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a passionate advocate who campaigns for a cause or idea, much like a crusader.

clue.text: Lines beginning to crack and split in street

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of the word crack
in places these pieces inside the abbreviation for the road

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
the opening letter of crack
a rip is a split or tear

explanation.surface: The pavement starts to crack and split open along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's lines are the words they speak, written in the script of a play or film.

clue.text: Person is very individual around setter

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the setter goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
one is a single individual
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A person is quite distinctive when compared with the compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' applies only to the word next to it, not to both 'very' and 'individual'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone means an unspecified human being, so the pronoun stands in for a person.

clue.text: Mock food

blocks.note: first meaning: jeer at or ridicule
second meaning: informal British slang for grub, things to eat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock food' reads like imitation food, but it is two separate meanings; in Britain scoff is informal slang for food and for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for jeering scornfully, and colloquially a noun for grub or eatables.

clue.text: Covers lump with sheets regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of sheets is kept

blocks.note: a clot is a lump of thickened matter, as of blood
the second, fourth and sixth letters of sheets

explanation.surface: A bed is made up with a lumpy bundle under the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' is a noun, not a verb: the things you wear over your body.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes are garments worn on the body, so they are coverings that protect and hide it.

clue.text: That man will love greeting

blocks.note: he will contracts to he'll
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A man will declare his love on meeting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the common word said when meeting or answering someone, an everyday salutation.

clue.text: Admit adult without good reason initially

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letters are taken away
initially points to the first letters of the words good and reason

blocks.note: a grown-up is an adult
the opening letters of good and reason

explanation.surface: An adult confesses to something without a proper excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G and R from the start of GROWNUP to leave the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess or acknowledge a fault, so the phrasal verb matches admit.

clue.text: Explosive I can still spark

indicators.note: something explosive blows apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone with a volatile temper boasts they can still ignite.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle, as in a spark of hope; the Latin word literally meant a spark.

clue.text: Mark allowed to swallow insides of neon bean

indicators.note: to swallow is to take something inside, so the pieces enclose the middle letters
the insides of a word are its letters without the ends, here of neon

blocks.note: to flag something is to mark it
let means allowed
the inner two letters of neon

explanation.surface: A marked sign is allowed to take in a neon bean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark allowed' works as one unit that opens up at the join to let the middle of neon in.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small pale green French kidney bean, eaten dried or fresh; it is also a kind of flute.

clue.text: Show much passion as endlessly downgraded

indicators.note: endlessly means with no ends, so the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: demoted means downgraded in rank

explanation.surface: Someone gets very worked up about being lowered in rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express feelings in an exaggerated, theatrical way, so it means displaying strong emotion.
